$comment: ESTIMATES, not measurements. Anthropic does not publish per-token energy or water figures. Energy is IT energy per 1,000 tokens (Wh) before PUE. 'low' and 'high' bound a plausible range; 'central' is the value shown by default. Override locally with <plugin data dir>/footprint.json.
assumptions: Output (decode) tokens dominate inference energy; published estimates for large models span roughly 0.1-2 Wh per 1,000 output tokens.
Uncached input (prefill) and cache writes are compute-bound and much cheaper per token than decode: assumed 1/20 to 1/5 of output.
Cache reads skip recomputation of the prefix: assumed 1/10 of uncached input.
PUE (facility overhead) 1.08-1.2, typical of hyperscale data centers.
Water = energy x (on-site cooling WUE + off-site water consumed to generate the electricity). Set water_scope=onsite to count cooling only, which is what most vendor per-prompt figures report.
No per-model size scaling is applied: a Haiku token and a Fable token use the same factors.

sources.title: Epoch AI estimate cited in 'Photons = Tokens' (arXiv 2603.06630): ~0.0001-0.002 Wh per output token
A Systematic Characterization of LLM Inference on GPUs (arXiv 2512.01644): decode dominates energy, ~1.7 J per generated token
From Words to Watts (arXiv 2310.03003): LLaMA-65B ~3-4 J per output token
How Hungry is AI? Energy, water and carbon of LLM inference (arXiv 2505.09598)
Making AI Less 'Thirsty' (Li et al., arXiv 2304.03271): on-site WUE plus off-site electricity water intensity
